title: Allow using functions as patterns
author: Delta-official
summary: Lets cssModules.pattern be a JS object `{resolve(hash, path, local, contentHash?), contentHash}`. The Rust `Pattern` struct becomes an enum with an `Arc<dyn PatternProvider>` variant. Every generated name then does a blocking cross-thread call into JS. It's a breaking change to the public Rust API and a new JS API, so it needs a product decision before any review.
evidence: Rust: `pub struct Pattern { segments }` -> `pub enum Pattern { Simple { segments }, Provider(Arc<dyn PatternProvider>) }`, and `Pattern::write` changes signature (breaking). The JS d.ts says `content_hash: boolean` but the napi code reads `contentHash`, so they don't match. The grid `[local]`-last check is skipped for providers (FIXME in the diff). No tests. It also includes unrelated rustfmt churn in selector.rs/bundler.rs, and the PR head is the fork's master branch. Related: #1237 (webpack-compatible hash patterns, where devongovett asked on 2026-05-17 "isn't the whole point of CSS modules that the scoped names are not predictable?"). #491 has no maintainer comment.
decision: Should Lightning CSS accept a JS callback for CSS modules names (a breaking Rust Pattern API change, plus a synchronous JS round trip per identifier), or keep patterns string-only?
